mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) implies an accommodative monetary policy, reducing the cost of capital and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This is most effective during monetary easing cycles.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns of SPX are negative in more than 60% of such periods over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.8% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a slowdown in corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises by more than 0.3 percentage points in 3 months, the 5-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline in the same month, the 20-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.5 during high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) signals an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 300 and INDPRO < 102.5, the 60-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL index above 302 indicates persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 302, the 20-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: Higher retail sales (RSAFS) indicate strong consumer spending, supporting corporate revenue growth and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days, especially during strong consumer demand regimes.
failure_condition: When RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, the 60-day forward returns of SPX are negative in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, leading to higher wage growth and inflation, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases in the same month, the 20-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of such months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.0 signals a manufacturing slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 102.0, the 5-day forward returns of SPX are positive in more than 60% of such periods.
